summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with dysuria, suprapubic abdominal pain, and new-onset confusion and myoclonus, following a recent urinary tract infection treated with ciprofloxacin. Given his history of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas infections and indwelling catheter, he was started on IV antibiotics. Brain imaging showed no acute pathology, with findings consistent with chronic changes. His symptoms improved rapidly, mental status normalized, and twitching resolved. Urine and blood cultures showed no growth. He was transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin and discharged back to the skilled nursing facility with plans for continued treatment and follow-up. His DNR status was reaffirmed.
